prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website composition probe for an Effective HTML catalog page, 16:10 landscape.
Reference image role: preserve the exact Working Atlas visual identity only — near-black Ink field, warm bone paper, cobalt, lilac, green, pink and coral flat printed inks, bold compressed grotesk, fine black rules, subtle paper tooth, slight controlled rotation, restrained shadows, crisp HTML geometry. Do not copy the existing landing-page composition.
Primary request: Design a complete catalog page using a PAIRED PROOF LEDGER composition. Thin site navigation at top. First viewport has a compact but bold title area reading exactly “Catalog” and a large featured specimen pairing: one HTML browser artifact beside its corresponding abstract SVG plate, clearly presented as two representations of the same idea. Below, show the start of a long editorial ledger where each specimen is a broad ruled row, not a card: oversized index number, category, artifact title, a generous preview, and compact actions for HTML, Static SVG, and Animated SVG. Include a small search field and three restrained source/filter controls. Make the relationship between source HTML and derived SVG instantly obvious. Uneven row heights and controlled asymmetry; one dense proof region and real quiet space.
Visible text: only “Effective HTML”, “Catalog”, “HTML”, “Static SVG”, and “Animated SVG” need be legible; all other copy should be short indistinct lines.
Constraints: this must read as a designed website interface, not a poster or physical desk scene. No generic equal card grid. No gradients, glass, glow, photographs, human hands, mascots, connector lines, dashboards, fake 3D chrome, or tiny paragraphs. Flat matte output, polished but implementable in semantic HTML/CSS, accessible hierarchy.
